label: <DEL> step of long sequences whose first token (to be output first) is in {c,e,x,f,3,q,d,v,1,s,z}
explanation: 97% of activation mass is at the delimiter step (t == L, recall_idx 0); it never fires in the copy phase and only weakly at the last 1-2 original steps of length-9 sequences. Rate rises steeply with L (none for L<=4, 12% of mass at L=7, 83% at L>=8). Within delimiter steps it is gated by the first original token (the token output at this step): c, e, x, f, 3 have the highest rates, then q, v, d, 1, s, z. The second original token (next_out) adds to it in the same direction: when both of the first two tokens are in the set, precision is about 0.83. Strongest activations are L=8-9 sequences that start with two tokens from the set (e f, f d, c 3, c v, e x). This looks like a graded sum over sequence length and the identities of the first one or two tokens, not a sharp rule, so the boolean predicate only reaches F1 of about 0.67.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: c, x, e, f, 3, q; least: g, k, i, a) and the next token to output (most: 3, d, f, e, x, c; least: n, g, o, a); timing cues that raise it most: t=7, t=8, L=9 & t=9.
